title: Implement locale-aware pairwise score harmonization and regression gates for rerank upgrades
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Recent experiments show that swapping cross-encoder variants for the reranking endpoint produces uneven utility across locales: some locales see small NDCG regressions while others improve, and raw pairwise scores are not comparable between model families. We need a deployment-safe upgrade path that preserves latency targets and reduces per-request cost while preventing quality regressions for high-impact customers.

Proposal summary: implement a locale-aware score harmonization layer combined with regression gates and an automated canary protocol. Instead of trying to normalize logits at inference time by brute-force rescoring, we will compute per-locale calibration mappings (monotonic transforms) between the candidate model family and the incumbent. At runtime a lightweight pairwise harmonizer will map scores from new variants into the incumbent score space; routing/threshold logic will use the harmonized value for selection and A/B canaries. For locales with large gaps we will fall back to incumbent or hybrid cross-attention fusion.

Key deliverables:
- calibration dataset and tooling (per-locale pairwise corpus with synthetic and production sampled queries)
- harmonization transform store + lightweight runtime mapping (O(1) cost per candidate)
- canary rollout orchestration with statistical regression gates (MRR/NDCG significance tests and latency p95/p99 checks)
- observability: per-locale quality dashboards, delta heatmaps, and automated alerts
- rollback/mitigation procedures (automatic fallback to incumbent model, traffic-level control)
acceptance_criteria:
1) Calibration dataset created for top 25 locales (CSV in S3) and documented in Confluence.
2) Harmonization library (Python + Rust shim) merged and callable from rerank service (PR merged).
3) Runtime mapping adds <0.5ms median overhead per candidate on current Dedicated nodes.
4) Canary automation performs significance test (two-sided bootstrap) on MRR/NDCG with alpha=0.05 and auto-rolls back on regression >0.005 absolute NDCG for a locale.
5) No customer-facing error increases in canary (error rate delta < 0.1%).
6) Dashboards capture per-locale NDCG, MRR, P50/P95/P99 latency and cost per 1k requests.
7) Runbook updated with mitigation steps and owner assigned.
notes:
Design choices and trade-offs:
- Why harmonize vs full retrain: harmonization allows rapid evaluation of many compact variants without retraining a large cross-encoder or expensive per-request rescoring; we accept some calibration noise but reduce iteration time.
- Mapping family: start with monotonic isotonic regression per-locale; if monotonic curve insufficient, add small piecewise-linear corrections per bucket.
- Fallbacks: hybrid fusion head (cheap cross-attention warm-start) reserved for high-impact locales where harmonization residuals exceed thresholds.
- SLO trade-offs: hitting p99 latency SLO will limit batch sizes and push some locales to dedicated paths; plan includes traffic shaping knob.

Metrics tracked: NDCG@10, MRR, pairwise-consistency rate, P50/P95/P99 latency, cost per 1k queries, delta-to-incumbent per-locale.
